transfer.name: Deed tax (recording privilege tax on deeds)
transfer.rateText: $.50 for each $500 or fraction thereof in value of property conveyed (Code of Ala. §40-22-1)
transfer.local: No local transfer tax add-on is set by §40-22-1; the tax is collected by the county judge of probate when the deed is recorded.

mortgageTax.name: Mortgage recording privilege tax
mortgageTax.note: $.15 for each $100 (or fraction) of the initial indebtedness secured (Code of Ala. §40-22-2).

transfer.notes: Only the value in excess of any mortgage or vendor's lien on which the mortgage tax has been paid is taxable under §40-22-1, so a deed recorded with a purchase-money mortgage is taxed on the price minus the loan. Proof of actual purchase price (or value) must accompany the deed.

income.cgNote: No special capital gains rate: gains are taxed as ordinary income at 2%-5%. Some Alabama cities/counties levy occupational taxes on wages, not on capital gains.
income.cgShort: graduated rates, gain taxed as income

transfer.rateText: No state transfer tax; the state Recorder's Office charges a recording fee only ($20 for the first page of a document, plus a fee per additional page; AS 40.17.030, 11 AAC 05.200)
transfer.local: No local real estate transfer tax found on official state sources; some boroughs and cities levy sales and property taxes (state DOR points to the 'Alaska Taxable' publication).

mortgageTax.note: A deed of trust pays only the per-page recording fee.

transfer.notes: Recording is done by the Department of Natural Resources Recorder's Office, not by counties.

income.cgNote: 'The State of Alaska currently does not have an individual income tax' (Alaska Department of Revenue).
income.cgShort: no personal income tax

transfer.rateText: No transfer tax; the county recorder collects a flat real estate transfer fee of $2 per deed or contract (A.R.S. §11-1132), with an affidavit of legal value
transfer.local: Arizona Constitution art. IX §24 bars the state, counties, cities and any district from imposing any new tax or fee on the sale or transfer of real property (anything not in existence on Dec. 31, 2007).

mortgageTax.note: No mortgage recording tax; the §11-1132 fee does not apply to transfers solely to provide or release security for a debt (A.R.S. §11-1134).

transfer.notes: Exemptions from the affidavit and fee include gift deeds, court-ordered conveyances and nominal-consideration transfers between spouses, parents and children (A.R.S. §11-1134).

income.cgNote: A.R.S. §43-1022(22): residents subtract 25% of net long-term capital gain included in federal AGI from assets acquired after Dec. 31, 2011 (not allowed if the acquisition date cannot be verified). Arizona starts from federal AGI, so the federal Section 121 home-sale exclusion carries over.
income.cgShort: 25% of a long-term gain subtracted

transfer.name: Real Property Transfer Tax
transfer.rateText: $3.30 per $1,000 of actual consideration on transactions that exceed $100 (Arkansas DFA)
transfer.local: No local add-on mentioned by DFA; the tax is evidenced by a Real Estate Transfer Document (stamp) bought from DFA / the county.

mortgageTax.note: No mortgage recording tax found on DFA pages; recording fees only.

transfer.notes: Also applies to transfers of ownership of mineral rights.

income.cgNote: Form AR1000D: only 50% of the Arkansas net capital gain is taxable, and net capital gain above $10,000,000 is excluded entirely (line 7b caps it at $10M). Arkansas adopts IRC §121: gain on the sale of a personal residence is exempt up to $250,000 per taxpayer ($500,000 married filing on the same return) under the 2-of-5-year rule. Short-term gains are fully taxable.
income.cgShort: half of a long-term gain taxed

transfer.name: Documentary Transfer Tax (county and city)
transfer.rateText: No state transfer tax. Under Rev. & Tax. Code §11911 a county may impose $0.55 for each $500 (or fraction) of consideration (0.11%), on value exclusive of liens remaining on the property; a city in that county may impose half that rate, credited against the county tax
transfer.local: County tax authorized at $0.55 per $500 (0.11% of price, net of liens remaining at sale); a city may levy $0.275 per $500, credited against the county tax (§11911(b)-(c)). Some charter cities (e.g. Los Angeles, San Francisco, Oakland, Berkeley) levy their own, much higher, real property transfer taxes under their charters, often graduated by price - check the city ordinance.

mortgageTax.note: No mortgage recording tax; deeds of trust pay county recording fees only.

transfer.notes: The county/city documentary transfer tax applies only when consideration exceeds $100 and excludes the value of any lien or encumbrance remaining on the property at the time of sale (assumed loans).

income.cgNote: 'California does not have a lower rate for capital gains. All capital gains are taxed as ordinary income' (FTB). Top regular rate 12.3% (2025: single over $742,953, joint over $1,485,906), plus the 1% Behavioral Health Services Tax (formerly Mental Health Services Tax) on taxable income above $1,000,000 = 13.3%.

surtax.note: Behavioral Health Services Tax: 1% of taxable income over $1,000,000 (same threshold for all filing statuses), confirmed in the 2026 Form 540-ES instructions.

income.cgShort: 1% more on income above $1,000,000

transfer.name: Documentary fee
transfer.rateText: Documentary fee of $0.01 per each hundred dollars of consideration, on a non-exempt deed transferring property when consideration is more than $500 (county clerk and recorder fee schedule; C.R.S. 39-13-102)
transfer.local: No county add-on beyond the documentary fee. A number of home-rule municipalities (mostly mountain resort towns) levy their own real estate transfer taxes by local ordinance; rates vary and are not set by state law.

mortgageTax.note: No mortgage recording tax; flat per-document recording fee ($43 per document since July 1, 2025 in Boulder County's schedule).

transfer.notes: The documentary fee is collected by the county clerk and recorder when the deed is recorded, along with a Real Property Transfer Declaration.

income.cgNote: Flat rate on Colorado taxable income, which starts from federal taxable income (so the federal Section 121 exclusion carries over). Since tax year 2022 the Colorado capital gain subtraction is limited to farmers (Schedule F filers) selling agricultural real property held 5+ years; it does not apply to a home sale.
income.cgShort: flat rate

uncertain: The 2026 rate is not yet published: the Department's table stops at 2025 (4.4%; 2024 was a temporary 4.25%). Colorado's rate can be lowered temporarily in a given year by TABOR surplus triggers.

Municipal real estate transfer taxes not compiled.

transfer.name: Real Estate Conveyance Tax (state portion)
transfer.rateText: Residential: 3/4 of 1% on the portion of consideration up to $800,000; 1 1/4% on the portion over $800,000 up to $2,500,000; 2 1/4% on the portion over $2,500,000 (C.G.S. §12-494(b)(2)(C)); applies when consideration is $2,000 or more
transfer.local: Municipal conveyance tax of 1/4 of 1% of the consideration in every municipality (§12-494(a)(2)); targeted investment communities and towns with designated manufacturing plants may add up to another 1/4 of 1% (§12-494(c)), i.e. up to 0.5% local.

mortgageTax.note: No mortgage recording tax; town clerk recording fees only.

transfer.notes: Non-residential property (other than unimproved land) is taxed at 1.25% for the state portion. Conveyances of delinquent-mortgage property to the lender are taxed at 0.75%. Revenue above $300M a year goes to the Housing Trust Fund from July 1, 2025.

income.cgNote: No special capital gains rate: gains are taxed as ordinary income (rates 2%-6.99% for tax years 2024 and later, C.G.S. §12-700(a)(10)). Connecticut starts from federal AGI, so the federal Section 121 home-sale exclusion carries over. High-income taxpayers also pay phase-out and 'benefit recapture' add-backs of the lower brackets (e.g. $50 per $5,000 of CT AGI over $500,000 for single filers, capped).
income.cgShort: graduated rates, gain taxed as income

transfer.name: Realty Transfer Tax (state portion)
transfer.rateText: 3 percent of the value of the property, unless the municipality or county has enacted the full 1 1/2 percent local realty transfer tax, in which case 2 1/2 percent (30 Del. C. §5402(a)); no tax when value is under $100
transfer.local: Counties (9 Del. C. §8102) and municipalities (22 Del. C. §1601) may levy up to 1 1/2 percent. Where the full local 1.5% is levied the state rate is 2.5% (total 4%); otherwise the state rate is 3%.
transfer.payerNote: 'Said tax is to be apportioned equally between grantor and grantee' (30 Del. C. §5402(a)).

mortgageTax.note: Mortgages are excluded from the definition of a taxable document (30 Del. C. §5401(1)c).

transfer.notes: First-time home buyer: the buyer's portion of the state tax is reduced by 1/2 percent times the lesser of the value or $400,000 (§5402(c)); the seller's half is not reduced. 'Value' includes assumed liens and is at least the highest appraised value unless lower fair market value is shown. Transfers between spouses, parent-child, siblings and grandparent-grandchild are exempt.

income.cgNote: No special capital gains rate: gains are taxed as ordinary income (2.2%-6.6%; 6.6% on taxable income over $60,000, 30 Del. C. §1102(a), schedule in force for taxable years after Dec. 31, 2013). Delaware starts from federal AGI, so the federal Section 121 exclusion carries over. Wilmington levies a city earned income tax on wages, not on capital gains.
income.cgShort: graduated rates, gain taxed as income

uncertain: Delaware joint filers use the same bracket thresholds (no doubling) per §1102 - joint threshold set to $60,000 from the same schedule; Delaware also allows spouses to file separately on a combined return.
Whether every county/municipality levies the full 1.5% (making 2.5% the typical state rate) was not checked county by county; the state rate is 3% where it does not.
Section 121 carry-over inferred from Delaware starting from federal AGI.

transfer.name: Deed recordation tax + real property transfer tax
transfer.rateText: Recordation tax 1.1% of the consideration (D.C. Code §42-1103(a)(1)) plus transfer tax 1.1% (§47-903(a)(1)); each gets an additional 0.35% except for residential properties transferred for a consideration less than $400,000 (§42-1103(a-4), §47-903(a-4)). Residential total: 2.2% under $400,000, 2.9% of the whole consideration at $400,000 or more
transfer.local: No separate local tax: the District is the only taxing level.
transfer.payerNote: Transfer tax: 'imposed on the transferor', with the transferee jointly and severally liable if the transferor fails to pay (§47-903(a)(1),(c)). The statute does not assign the recordation tax to one party, but the first-time homebuyer reduction must benefit the grantees (buyers).

mortgageTax.name: Recordation tax on security interest instruments
mortgageTax.note: A purchase-money deed of trust recorded with the deed is exempt (§42-1102(5)). Other security instruments (e.g. refinances, on new money only) are taxed at 1.1% of the debt secured (§42-1103(a)(3)).

transfer.notes: First-time DC homebuyers who qualify get a reduced recordation tax rate of 0.725% for a deed of title (§42-1103), with the benefit going to the buyer; eligibility conditions (income, price) are in the statute. Transfers of an economic interest (controlling interest) are taxed at 2.9% recordation. Non-residential property pays the +0.35% at any price.

income.cgNote: No special capital gains rate: gains are taxed as ordinary income under the schedule for tax years beginning after 12/31/2021 (4%-10.75%; 10.75% over $1,000,000, same brackets for all filing statuses). DC starts from federal AGI, so the federal Section 121 exclusion carries over.
income.cgShort: graduated rates, gain taxed as income

transfer.name: Documentary Stamp Tax on deeds
transfer.rateText: 70 cents on each $100 or portion thereof of the total consideration, in all counties except Miami-Dade (s. 201.02(1)(a), F.S.); Miami-Dade: 60 cents per $100, plus a 45-cent surtax per $100 that is not due on a document transferring only a single-family dwelling (s. 201.031, F.S.)
transfer.local: Miami-Dade County: 0.60% instead of 0.70%, plus 0.45% surtax except on single-family dwellings. No other local add-on.
transfer.payerNote: 'All parties to the document are liable for the tax regardless of which party agrees to pay the tax' (Florida DOR); if one party is exempt the non-exempt party must pay.

mortgageTax.name: Documentary stamp tax on notes/mortgages (0.35%) + nonrecurring intangible tax (0.2%)
mortgageTax.note: Doc stamp tax on mortgages and the debt they secure: 35 cents per $100 or portion thereof of the amount secured, no cap for recorded mortgages (s. 201.08, F.S.); the $2,450 cap applies only to notes not secured by a recorded mortgage. Nonrecurring intangible tax: 2 mills (0.2%) of the obligation secured by Florida real property (s. 199.133, F.S.).

transfer.notes: Consideration includes any mortgage assumed. Transfers of homestead between spouses where the only consideration is a mortgage are exempt (s. 201.02(7)(b)). Tax is paid to the county clerk/recording official at recording.

income.cgNote: Florida Constitution art. VII §5(a): no tax upon the income of natural persons who are residents or citizens of the state (beyond amounts creditable against federal tax). No state tax on a home-sale gain.
income.cgShort: no personal income tax

transfer.name: Real Estate Transfer Tax
transfer.rateText: $1 for the first $1,000 or fractional part of $1,000 and 10 cents for each additional $100 or fractional part of $100 of the sale price (O.C.G.A. 48-6-1 to 48-6-10)
transfer.local: No local add-on; the tax is paid to the clerk of the superior court of the county before the deed is recorded (Form PT-61 declaration).
transfer.payerNote: 'The seller is liable for the real estate transfer tax, though frequently the parties agree in the sales contract that the buyer will pay the tax' (Georgia DOR).

mortgageTax.name: Intangible recording tax
mortgageTax.note: $1.50 for each $500 or fractional part of the face amount of the note secured by Georgia real estate; maximum $25,000 per note. Collected from the holder of the security instrument (lender), who may pass it on to the borrower.

transfer.notes: No mansion tax or first-time buyer reduction found on DOR pages.

income.cgNote: Flat 4.99% for 2026 (down from 5.19%), standard deduction $15,000 single / $30,000 joint (Georgia DOR, 2026 Income Tax Changes). No special capital gains rate. Georgia starts from federal AGI, so the federal Section 121 exclusion carries over.
income.cgShort: flat rate

transfer.name: Conveyance Tax
transfer.rateText: Rate per $100 of the actual and full consideration, applied to the whole price according to the property's value: $.10 under $600,000; $.20 $600,000-$999,999; $.30 $1M-$1,999,999; $.50 $2M-$3,999,999; $.70 $4M-$5,999,999; $.90 $6M-$9,999,999; $1.00 at $10M or more. Higher schedule for a condominium or single-family residence whose purchaser is ineligible for a county homeowner's exemption: $.15 / $.25 / $.40 / $.60 / $.85 / $1.10 / $1.25 per $100. Minimum $1
transfer.local: No county add-on; the tax is state-wide (HRS chapter 247), paid with Form P-64A.
transfer.payerNote: 'The person subject to the conveyance tax is generally the grantor, lessor, sublessor, assignor, transferor, seller, conveyor' (Form P-64A instructions).

mortgageTax.note: No mortgage recording tax found; Bureau of Conveyances recording fees only.

transfer.notes: Non-owner-occupant schedule (purchaser ineligible for the county homeowner's exemption) on condos and single-family homes: 0.15% under $600k, 0.25%, 0.40%, 0.60%, 0.85%, 1.10%, 1.25% at $10M+ (whole-price). Consideration includes liens or encumbrances on the property at the time of sale.

income.cgNote: Net long-term capital gain is taxed at a maximum of 7.25% (alternative tax, Form N-11 instructions); ordinary income up to 11%.
income.cgShort: long-term gain taxed at 7.25% at most

transfer.name: Real Estate Transfer Tax (Illinois tax stamps)
transfer.rateText: Illinois tax stamps: net consideration divided by $500 (rounded up to the next whole number) multiplied by $0.50, i.e. $0.50 per $500 (PTAX-203 line 19)
transfer.local: County tax stamps add $0.25 per $500 (0.05%) (PTAX-203 line 20, all counties). Home-rule units such as Cook County and the City of Chicago file their own transfer declarations and levy their own additional transfer taxes (amounts not read on an official source here).

mortgageTax.note: No state mortgage recording tax found on the Illinois Department of Revenue forms; county recording fees only.

transfer.notes: Tax is computed on net consideration (Line 17: full consideration minus personal property and the amount of an assumed mortgage/exempt amounts); transfers listed in 35 ILCS 200/31-45 are exempt (PTAX-203 line 16).

income.cgNote: Capital gains taxed as ordinary income at the flat 4.95%. IL-1040 starts from federal adjusted gross income (line 1), so the federal Section 121 home-sale exclusion ($250,000/$500,000) carries over.

transfer.notes: Consideration includes an assumed encumbrance; personal property stated on the instrument is deducted. A declaration of value must accompany the deed; exemptions are listed in §428A.2.

transfer.name: Real Estate Transfer Tax
transfer.rateText: $2.20 for each $500 or fractional part of $500 of the value of the property transferred; when the value exceeds $1,000,000, an additional $3.80 for each $500 or fractional part of $500 of the value that exceeds $1,000,000 (36 M.R.S. §4641-A, text effective 11/01/25)

transfer.payerNote: 36 M.R.S. §4641-A(1)(B): 'The tax is imposed 1/2 on the grantor and 1/2 on the grantee.'
transfer.notes: Since November 1, 2025 the slice of value above $1,000,000 bears an extra $3.80 per $500 (0.76%), i.e. 1.2% in total on that slice. The same rates apply to the transfer of a controlling interest in an entity owning Maine real property (§4641-A(2)).

income.cgNote: Capital gains taxed as ordinary income. 2026 brackets: single 5.8% under $27,400, 6.75% to $64,850, 7.15% above; joint 5.8% under $54,850, 6.75% to $129,750, 7.15% above.

surtax.note: From tax year 2026, a 2% surcharge on Maine taxable income above $1,000,000 (single), $750,000 (married filing separately) or $1,500,000 (married filing jointly or head of household); thresholds indexed from 2027.

income.cgShort: 2% surcharge on income above $1,000,000 single, $1,500,000 joint

uncertain: Maine's starting point (federal AGI, which would carry the Section 121 home-sale exclusion) not read on an official Maine page.

transfer.name: State Transfer Tax
transfer.rateText: The rate of the transfer tax is 0.5% of the consideration payable for the instrument of writing (Tax-Property §13-203(a)); 0.25% for a sale of improved residential property to a first-time Maryland home buyer who will occupy it as a principal residence, paid entirely by the seller (§13-203(b)(3))
transfer.local: Counties and Baltimore City set their own recordation tax rate per $500 of consideration (Tax-Property §12-103(b)), and many also levy a county transfer tax; rates vary by county and are not uniform. Counties may exempt part of the consideration for owner-occupied principal residences or first-time buyers.
transfer.payerNote: For a first-time Maryland home buyer purchase, the reduced 0.25% state transfer tax 'shall be paid entirely by the seller' (§13-203(b)(3)); otherwise the statute read does not allocate the tax.

mortgageTax.name: Recordation tax (county rate)
mortgageTax.note: County recordation tax rates apply to each $500 of consideration payable or of the principal amount of the debt secured (Tax-Property §12-103(a)); rate set by each county, so no statewide figure.

transfer.notes: First-time Maryland home buyer (never owned a Maryland principal residence; all grantees must qualify) pays 0.25% state rate instead of 0.5%, borne by the seller. The 0.5% rate also applies to transfers of a controlling interest in certain LIHTC real property entities.

income.cgNote: Graduated 2%-6.5% (single: 5.75% to $500,000, 6.25% $500,001-$1,000,000, 6.5% above; joint: 6.25% $600,001-$1,200,000, 6.5% above). Plus county income tax of 2.25% to 3.30% of Maryland taxable income (Tax-General §10-106). An additional 2% applies to net capital gain when federal AGI exceeds $350,000, but a gain on a primary-residence single-family home, townhouse, row home, condo or co-op sold for less than $1,500,000 is exempt from that additional 2%.
income.cgShort: county income tax on top; extra 2% above $350,000 of income, not on a main home sold under $1.5M

County recordation and county transfer tax rates not compiled (vary by county); payer by custom not stated officially.

Whether the $350,000 threshold is the same for joint filers: the statute says 'federal adjusted gross income in excess of $350,000' for individuals in paragraphs (1) or (2) without a separate joint figure.

transfer.name: Deeds Excise
transfer.rateText: Deeds: sales price (less mortgage assumed) of real estate, $2.28 per $500 (DOR Tax Rates page); i.e. $2.00 per $500 plus a 14% surtax
transfer.local: Barnstable County has a different deeds excise rate (DOR Directive 95-4: 'except for Barnstable county'); the current Barnstable figure was not read on an official page.
transfer.payerNote: DOR Directive 95-4: the deeds excise is self-assessed and paid by the person who makes or signs the deed (the grantor), G.L. c. 64D, § 2.
transfer.notes: Due on consideration in excess of $100; an assumed mortgage is deducted from the price. No first-time buyer reduction or mansion rate found on the DOR rate page.

income.cgNote: Long-term capital gains taxed at 5.00%; short-term capital gains at 8.5%; long-term gains on collectibles 12% (50% deduction). The 4% surtax on income above $1,107,750 (tax year 2026) comes on top (9% combined on long-term gains above the threshold). The surtax threshold is the same amount for single and joint returns (each return).

surtax.note: Tax year 2026: additional 4% surtax on income exceeding $1,107,750 (2025: $1,083,150; 2024: $1,053,750).

income.cgShort: 4% surtax on income above $1,107,750

transfer.name: State Real Estate Transfer Tax (SRETT)
transfer.rateText: $3.75 for each $500, or fraction of $500, of the total value of the property (MCL 207.525)
transfer.local: County real estate transfer tax (Public Act 134 of 1966): $0.55 per $500 of consideration (0.11%), as published by Oakland County Register of Deeds and Mackinac County; total state + county = $4.30 per $500 (0.86%).
transfer.payerNote: Michigan Treasury: 'The seller (grantor) is legally responsible for paying SRETT'; some buyers and sellers agree that the buyer pays on the seller's behalf.
transfer.notes: Principal residence exemption (MCL 207.526(u)): a seller can obtain a refund of SRETT (Form 2796, within four years and 15 days) on the sale of a principal residence when its conditions are met, which include proof of the SEV at purchase and in the year of sale. Transfers under $100 are exempt.

income.cgNote: Capital gains taxed as ordinary income at the flat 4.25% (Treasury notice of April 15, 2026: no formula reduction for 2026). Federal AGI is the starting point of the Michigan return, so the federal Section 121 home-sale exclusion carries over. Some cities levy their own income tax on residents.
income.cgShort: flat rate

transfer.name: Deed Tax
transfer.rateText: When the consideration, exclusive of any lien or encumbrance remaining at the time of sale, exceeds $3,000, the tax is .0033 of the net consideration; $1.65 when it is $3,000 or less (Minn. Stat. §287.21, subd. 1)
transfer.local: Hennepin County and Ramsey County may impose an additional deed tax of .0001 of the amount (0.01%) and an additional mortgage registry tax of .0001 of the principal (Minn. Stat. §383B.80 and §383A.80), giving 0.34% deed tax and 0.24% mortgage registry tax there.

mortgageTax.name: Mortgage Registry Tax
mortgageTax.note: A tax on the privilege of recording a mortgage at .0023 of the debt secured; the person liable is the mortgagor (Minn. Stat. §287.035). Plus .0001 in Hennepin and Ramsey counties.

transfer.notes: The deed tax applies to net consideration (excluding liens or encumbrances remaining on the property). Entity conversions are not treated as conveyances.

income.cgNote: Capital gains taxed as ordinary income. 2026 brackets: single 5.35% to $33,310, 6.80% to $109,430, 7.85% to $203,150, 9.85% above; married filing jointly 5.35% to $48,700, 6.80% to $193,480, 7.85% to $337,930, 9.85% above. The 1% net investment income tax excludes the gain on property classified as class 2a (agricultural), not an ordinary home.

surtax.note: Net investment income tax: 1% on net investment income (IRC §1411(c) definition, excluding gain on class 2a property) above $1,000,000 (Minn. Stat. §290.033); same threshold for all filers per the statute text.

income.cgShort: 1% on investment income above $1,000,000

transfer.rateText: No state real estate transfer tax; chancery clerk recording fees only
transfer.local: No county transfer tax identified.

A home-sale gain that is taxable federally (above the Section 121 exclusion) is therefore not taxed by Missouri. Ordinary income remains taxed at graduated rates (RSMo 143.011: top rate 4.95% from 2023, with possible annual reductions).
income.cgShort: 100% of capital gains subtracted since 2025

transfer.rateText: No real estate transfer tax: Montana Constitution Art. VIII, Sec. 17 provides that the state or any local government unit may not impose any tax, including a sales tax, on the sale or transfer of real property.
transfer.local: Local governments are also barred by the same constitutional provision (CI-105, approved Nov. 2, 2010).

mortgageTax.note: No state mortgage recording/intangible tax identified; only ordinary county recording fees.

transfer.notes: A realty transfer certificate is filed with the deed for property-valuation purposes, but no tax is charged on the transfer.

income.cgNote: Net long-term capital gains are taxed at separate rates (MCA 15-30-2103, version through Dec. 31, 2026): 3.0% on the portion of capital gains up to $47,500 single / $95,000 joint (and $71,250 head of household) less nonqualified (ordinary) taxable income, 4.1% above. Ordinary income: 4.7% then 5.65%. From tax year 2027 the ordinary top rate falls to 5.4% above $65,000 single / $130,000 joint; capital gains rates stay 3.0%/4.1%. Montana taxable income starts from federal income, so the federal Section 121 home-sale exclusion carries through.
income.cgShort: separate 3% and 4.1% rates on long-term gains

transfer.name: Documentary Stamp Tax
transfer.rateText: As of July 18, 2026, $3.32 for each $1,000 of value (or fraction thereof) of the real estate transferred (Neb. Rev. Stat. § 76-901); value divided by 1,000 is rounded up to the next whole number.
transfer.local: No separate local transfer tax; the state tax is collected by each county's register of deeds.
transfer.payerNote: Nebraska DOR: the tax is imposed on the grantor executing a deed.

mortgageTax.note: No mortgage recording/intangible tax identified on the DOR documentary stamp tax page.

transfer.notes: The rate rose to $3.32 per $1,000 on July 18, 2026. Exemptions are claimed with the Certificate of Exemption (e.g. deeds to trustees, family corporation/partnership/LLC transfers); Form 521 Real Estate Transfer Statement is filed with the deed.

income.cgNote: No general capital gains preference: gains are taxed as ordinary income (2026 brackets 2.46%, 3.51%, 4.55%; the 3rd and 4th brackets are both 4.55% per Neb. Rev. Stat. § 77-2715.03(2)(c)(v)). Nebraska's special capital gains deduction applies only to employer stock, not to a home sale. Nebraska starts from federal AGI, so the federal Section 121 home-sale exclusion carries through.
income.cgShort: graduated rates, gain taxed as income

uncertain: Top bracket start is from the DOR 2026 Estimated Income Tax Rate Schedule (Form 1040N-ES), which DOR says is for estimates only; the final 2026 tax return schedule was not yet published.

transfer.name: Real Property Transfer Tax
transfer.rateText: NRS 375.023: $1.30 per $500 of value or fraction thereof (state, deposited in the State General Fund) plus NRS 375.020: $1.25 per $500 in a county of 700,000+ population (Clark) or 65 cents per $500 in other counties. Base total outside Clark County $1.95 per $500 (0.39%); Clark County $2.55 per $500 (0.51%).
transfer.local: Counties under 700,000 population may add up to 5 cents per $500 (NRS 375.026). Washoe County Recorder states a total rate of $2.05 per $500 (0.41%); Clark County Recorder states $2.55 per $500 (0.51%).
transfer.payerNote: NRS 375.030(2): the buyer and seller are jointly and severally liable for the tax; the escrow holder is not liable. Allocation between them is left to the contract.

mortgageTax.note: No mortgage recording/intangible tax in NRS chapter 375; only county recording fees.

transfer.notes: Tax applies when consideration or value exceeds $100 and is based on the declared value (Declaration of Value form, NRS 375.060); exemptions are listed in NRS 375.090.

income.cgNote: Nevada Constitution Art. 10, Sec. 1(9): no income tax shall be levied upon the wages or personal income of natural persons; capital gains of individuals are therefore not taxed by the state.
income.cgShort: no personal income tax

transfer.name: Real Estate Transfer Tax
transfer.rateText: $.75 per $100 of the price or consideration (or fractional part thereof), imposed on both the buyer and the seller (RSA 78-B:1 and 78-B:4 III) — 0.75% each, 1.5% combined; minimum tax $20 where the price is $4,000 or less; computed to the nearest whole dollar.
transfer.local: No local transfer tax; the state tax is collected through the county registers of deeds.
transfer.payerNote: NH DRA: the tax is imposed on both the buyer and the seller at $.75 per $100 each (RSA 78-B:4 I-III).

mortgageTax.note: No mortgage recording/intangible tax identified in RSA 78-B.

transfer.notes: Every transfer of real estate or of an interest in real estate, including transfers by operation of law, is presumed taxable unless exempt under RSA 78-B:2; transfers of interests in entities owning real estate can be taxable. Buyer and seller each file a declaration of consideration (RSA 78-B:10).

income.cgNote: NH DRA: New Hampshire does not have an income tax on W-2 wages; the Interest and Dividends Tax (3% for periods ending on or after Dec. 31, 2024) was repealed for taxable periods beginning after December 31, 2024 (TIR 2025-001). Individuals' capital gains were never within the I&D tax and are not taxed in 2026.
income.cgShort: no tax on wages or capital gains

The statement that capital gains were never within the I&D tax is from the tax's name/definition, not quoted from the DRA page; the DRA page confirms only wages are untaxed and I&D repealed. Business Profits Tax on sole proprietors' business income is outside scope.

transfer.name: Realty Transfer Fee (RTF) + Graduated Percent Fee over $1 million
transfer.local: No separate county or municipal transfer tax is described by the Division of Taxation; the RTF and Graduated Percent Fee are paid when the deed is recorded with the county recording officer.
transfer.payerNote: NJ Division of Taxation: the State imposes the RTF on the seller; the seller is statutorily responsible for both the RTF and the Graduated Percent Fee.

mortgageTax.note: No mortgage recording tax; deeds given solely to provide security for a debt are exempt from the RTF.

transfer.notes: Graduated Percent Fee (former buyer-paid 1% 'mansion tax'), since July 10, 2025 (P.L. 2025, c. 69) imposed on the seller and applied to the WHOLE consideration ('whole' mode) for Class 2 residential, Class 3A farm with residence, Class 4A commercial and Class 4C co-op: 1% over $1,000,000 to $2,000,000; 2% over $2,000,000 to $2,500,000; 2.5% over $2,500,000 to $3,000,000; 3% over $3,000,000 to $3,500,000; 3.5% over $3,500,000 (e.g. $2.75M → 2.5% × $2.75M = $68,750). Reduced RTF schedule for senior citizens, blind or disabled persons and low/moderate income housing (per $500: $0.50/$1.25 when ≤$350,000; $1.40/$2.15/$2.65/$3.15/$3.40 when over $350,000). A Controlling Interest Transfer Tax applies to certain entity transfers.

income.cgNote: Capital gains are taxed as ordinary income (rates 1.4% to 10.75%; 8.97% from $500,000 to $1,000,000). NJ computes the gain the same way as for federal purposes and allows the principal residence exclusion based on federal guidelines: up to $250,000 ($500,000 married filing jointly), with a reduced exclusion where the federal rules allow it. Nonresident sellers may owe an estimated tax payment at closing (GIT/REP forms).
income.cgShort: graduated rates, gain taxed as income

transfer.local: No county or municipal real estate transfer tax identified.

For a home sale this generally means only the $2,500 deduction (half each for married filing separately). Before 2025 it was the greater of $1,000 or 40% of net capital gains. Rates (NMSA 7-2-7, tax years beginning on or after Jan. 1, 2025): 1.5%, 3.2%, 4.3%, 4.7%, 4.9%, 5.9%. NM starts from federal AGI, so the federal Section 121 home-sale exclusion carries through.
income.cgShort: home sale gain deduction limited to $2,500

transfer.name: Real Estate Transfer Tax
transfer.rateText: Two dollars for each $500, or fractional part thereof, of consideration (0.4%), on conveyances where consideration exceeds $500. Additional tax (mansion tax): 1% of the sale price of residences where consideration is $1 million or more (whole price, paid by buyer).
transfer.local: New York City (since July 1, 2019): additional base tax of $1.25 per $500 (0.25%, total base 0.65%) when consideration for residential property is $3 million or more (seller), plus a buyer-paid supplemental tax on residential conveyances of $2 million or more applied to the entire consideration: 0.25% ($2M–<$3M), 0.5% ($3M–<$5M), 1.25% ($5M–<$10M), 2.25% ($10M–<$15M), 2.5% ($15M–<$20M), 2.75% ($20M–<$25M), 2.9% ($25M+). New York City also levies its own Real Property Transfer Tax, and some localities levy local transfer taxes; these are not described on the DTF page and were not verified.
transfer.payerNote: NY DTF: the base tax and additional base tax are paid by the grantor (seller) — the buyer pays only if the seller fails to pay or is exempt, or by contract; the mansion tax and NYC supplemental tax are paid by the buyer (seller liable if the buyer fails to pay or is exempt).

mortgageTax.name: Mortgage Recording Tax
mortgageTax.note: State: basic tax 50 cents per $100 (0.5%) + special additional tax 25 cents per $100 (0.25%) + additional tax 25 cents per $100 (0.25%; 30 cents/0.30% in the Metropolitan Commuter Transportation District, unless suspended in the county; first $10,000 of debt deducted for 1–2 family residences) = 1.0% outside the MCTD, 1.05% within it. New York City, Yonkers and various counties add 25 to 50 cents per $100; rates by jurisdiction are on Form MT-15.

transfer.notes: Mansion tax (1%) is computed on the whole price once consideration is $1 million or more ('whole' mode); NYC additional base tax (0.25%, residential ≥ $3M) and the NYC supplemental tax rate also apply to the entire consideration. Transfers or acquisitions of a controlling interest in an entity owning real property are taxable on apportioned fair market value.

income.cgNote: No capital gains preference: gains are taxed as ordinary income under the 2026 schedule (3.90% to 10.9%; 6.85% from $215,400 single / $323,200 joint, 9.65% from $1,077,550 single / $2,155,350 joint, 10.3% from $5,000,000, 10.9% above $25,000,000). Above certain NYAGI thresholds the benefit of lower brackets is recaptured (flat-rate computation). New York City residents also pay NYC personal income tax (top 3.876% for 2026). NY starts from federal AGI, so the federal Section 121 home-sale exclusion carries through; nonresident sellers make an estimated income tax payment at transfer (IT-2663) unless exempt.
income.cgShort: graduated rates, gain taxed as income

transfer.local: Proceeds are split half to the county general fund and half to the State. A few counties levy their own local land transfer tax under local acts; those rates were not verified on an official source in this session.

income.cgShort: flat rate

transfer.local: No local real estate transfer tax identified.

mortgageTax.note: No mortgage recording/registry tax identified; only recording fees.

transfer.name: Real Property Conveyance Fee (county auditor fee R.C. 319.54(G)(3) + county real property transfer tax R.C. 322.02)
transfer.rateText: Statewide mandatory fee for receiving statements of value (R.C. 319.54(G)(3)): one dollar, or ten cents for each one hundred dollars or fraction of one hundred dollars (0.1%), whichever is greater, of the value of the real property transferred. Counties may add a real property transfer tax of up to thirty cents per one hundred dollars (0.3%) (R.C. 322.02), for a maximum combined 0.4%.
transfer.local: Each county may levy, by resolution of the board of county commissioners after two public hearings, a real property transfer tax at a uniform rate not to exceed 30 cents per $100 of value (R.C. 322.02(A)); county rates vary and were not compiled here.
transfer.payerNote: R.C. 322.02(A): the county real property transfer tax is levied upon the grantor named in the deed and paid by the grantor to the county auditor before the deed is presented to the recorder. The payer of the 0.1% auditor fee is not stated in the text of 319.54(G)(3) read.

mortgageTax.note: No mortgage recording/intangible tax identified; only recorder fees.

transfer.notes: No fee is charged on transfers to or from the United States, Ohio or its subdivisions, or made solely to provide or release security for a debt, or to confirm/correct a recorded deed, among other exemptions listed in R.C. 319.54(G)(3).

income.cgNote: No capital gains preference for individuals: gains are nonbusiness income taxed under the regular schedule (2025: 0% up to $26,050; $342 + 2.75% of excess over $26,050 up to $100,000; $2,394.32 + 3.125% of excess over $100,000; same brackets for all filing statuses). Business income is taxed at a flat 3%. Ohio starts from federal AGI, so the federal Section 121 home-sale exclusion carries through.
income.cgShort: graduated rates, gain taxed as income

Ohio statutes (R.C. 319.54, 322.02) read on Internet Archive copies (2025) because codes.ohio.gov refused connections.
Combined county rates (many counties at the 0.3% maximum, giving 0.4% total) not verified county by county.

transfer.name: Documentary Stamp Tax
transfer.rateText: Seventy-five cents ($0.75) for each Five Hundred Dollars ($500.00) of the consideration or any fractional part thereof (68 O.S. § 3201), on deeds conveying realty sold when consideration (exclusive of liens remaining) exceeds $100.
transfer.local: No separate local transfer tax; stamps are sold by the county clerks for the Oklahoma Tax Commission (68 O.S. § 3204).
transfer.payerNote: 68 O.S. § 3203(A): the tax shall be paid by any person who makes, signs, issues or sells the deed, or for whose use or benefit it is made — the statute does not assign it to the buyer or seller specifically.

mortgageTax.name: Mortgage Registration Tax
mortgageTax.note: 68 O.S. § 1904(A): ten cents per $100 (0.1%) of the principal debt where the mortgage is for five years or more; 8 cents (4–5 years), 6 cents (3–4 years), 4 cents (2–3 years), 2 cents (under 2 years); plus a $10 county treasurer certification fee per mortgage. May be paid by the mortgagor, the mortgagee or any other interested party.

transfer.notes: Consideration includes any assumed indebtedness but excludes liens remaining on the property; exemptions in 68 O.S. § 3202 (e.g. deeds securing a debt, confirmatory deeds, certain family transfers without consideration).

income.cgNote: Capital gain deduction (68 O.S. § 2358(F)): individuals may deduct 'qualifying gains receiving capital treatment', including net capital gains from the sale of real property located in Oklahoma owned for a holding period of at least five years — so the gain on an Oklahoma home held 5+ years is fully deductible; otherwise gains are taxed as ordinary income. 2026 rates (68 O.S. § 2355(D)): single 0% on first $3,750, 2.5% on next $1,150, 3.5% on next $2,300, 4.5% on the remainder (above $7,200); joint/head of household 0% on first $7,500, 2.5% on next $2,300, 3.5% on next $4,600, 4.5% above $14,400. Rates may fall by 0.25 point steps under revenue triggers (§ 2355(E)). Oklahoma starts from federal AGI, so the Section 121 exclusion carries through.
income.cgShort: gain on Oklahoma real estate held 5 years or more is deductible

uncertain: Read from the Oklahoma Legislature's complete Title 68 PDF (includes Laws 2025 amendments effective Nov. 1, 2025). Whether a trigger-based 0.25-point reduction applies for 2026 was not checked (Board of Equalization certification).
Oklahoma Tax Commission pages on the documentary stamp tax were not found on oklahoma.gov/tax.

transfer.rateText: No state real estate transfer tax. Washington County levies a county Real Property Transfer Tax of one dollar per thousand dollars of the selling price (0.1%).
transfer.local: Washington County (Washington County Code chapter 3.04, 'Real Property Transfer Tax Ordinance'): $1 per $1,000 of the selling price (0.1%), with exemptions applied for in writing within 15 days of tender for recording. No other county or city transfer tax was verified.

mortgageTax.note: No mortgage recording/intangible tax identified.

income.cgNote: No general capital gains preference: gains are taxed as ordinary income (2025 charts: 8.75% from $50,000 to $125,000 single / $250,000 joint, 9.9% above). Oregon DOR: Oregon follows federal law on the gain from the sale of a residence and won't tax gains of $500,000 or less ($250,000 married filing separately) if the federal qualifications are met. A separate farm asset capital gain method applies only to qualifying farm assets.
income.cgShort: graduated rates, gain taxed as income

transfer.name: Realty Transfer Tax
transfer.rateText: 1 percent on the value of real estate (including contracted-for improvements) transferred by deed, instrument, long-term lease or other writing (state); an additional local realty transfer tax is often collected with it.
transfer.local: Local realty transfer taxes are collected by the county Recorders of Deeds together with the state 1%; locals may share their tax among school districts and municipalities. Local rates vary by municipality/school district and were not verified (no uniform statutory figure on the Department of Revenue page).
transfer.payerNote: PA Department of Revenue: both grantor and grantee are held jointly and severally liable for payment of the tax; the split is left to the parties.

mortgageTax.note: No mortgage recording/intangible tax identified.

transfer.notes: Exempt transfers include certain transfers among family members, to governmental units, between religious organizations, to shareholders or partners, to/from nonprofit industrial development agencies, burial sites, certain transfers of ownership in real estate companies and farms, and property passed by will or intestacy. 15% of collections go to the Keystone Recreation, Park and Conservation Fund.

income.cgNote: Flat 3.07%; net gains from the disposition of property are one of eight income classes (no standard deduction or personal exemption; losses cannot offset other classes or be carried over). PA does NOT use the federal Section 121 computation: it has its own principal residence exclusion for sales after Dec. 31, 1997 — the seller must have owned and used the home as principal residence for at least 2 of the 5 years before sale and not sold another principal residence within the prior 2 years (unforeseen change in employment, health or severe financial hardship excepted). The REV-625 brochure states no dollar cap; on a joint PA return both spouses qualify if one spouse meets the requirements. Gain on portions used for business/rental or for which office-in-home depreciation was allowable is not excluded; non-qualifying gain is reported on PA Schedule D (PA-19 worksheet).
income.cgShort: own home sale exclusion (2 of 5 years), no dollar cap

transfer.name: Realty Conveyance Tax
transfer.rateText: Since October 1, 2025: Tier 1 $3.75 for each $500 or fractional part of the entire consideration (0.75%); Tier 2 an additional $3.75 per $500 (0.75%) on the consideration paid for residential real property in excess of $800,000, so 1.5% on the slice above $800,000 (R.I. Gen. Laws § 44-25-1(a)-(b); ADV 2025-13). Before Oct. 1, 2025 both tiers were $2.30 per $500.
transfer.local: No separate local conveyance tax; part of the state tax ($1.80 of each $3.75 in Tier 1) is distributed to the city or town.
transfer.payerNote: R.I. Gen. Laws § 44-25-1(a): in the absence of an agreement to the contrary, the tax shall be paid by the grantor.

mortgageTax.note: No mortgage recording tax found in chapter 44-25.

transfer.notes: The $800,000 Tier 2 threshold is adjusted for inflation (CPI-U) from January 1, 2026, rounded up to the nearest $5, never decreasing; the 2026 figure was not found. The tax also applies to transfers of interests in an acquired real estate company (controlling-interest rule).

income.cgNote: Tax year 2025 brackets (same for all filing statuses): 3.75% up to $79,900, 4.75% to $181,650, 5.99% over $181,650. Capital gains are taxed as ordinary income (no special rate or exclusion found in the instructions). Rhode Island starts from federal AGI, so the federal § 121 home-sale exclusion carries through.
income.cgShort: graduated rates, gain taxed as income

transfer.name: Deed Recording Fee
transfer.rateText: $1.85 for each $500, or fractional part of $500, of the realty's value (S.C. Code § 12-24-10), made of a state fee of $1.30 per $500 and a county fee of $0.55 per $500 (§ 12-24-90)
transfer.local: The $1.85 per $500 already includes the county share ($0.55 per $500, credited to the county general fund under § 12-24-90); the statute sets no other uniform local deed fee. Ordinary per-document recording charges of the register of deeds apply in addition.
transfer.payerNote: S.C. Code § 12-24-20: the fee is the liability of the grantor (seller); the grantee is secondarily liable.

mortgageTax.note: Chapter 24 of Title 12 imposes the fee on deeds only; no state mortgage recording tax was found in the statute.

transfer.notes: Value is the consideration paid or to be paid (§ 12-24-30). § 12-24-40 lists exempt deeds (e.g. transfers to a family trust or partnership without consideration, corrective deeds, deeds in lieu of foreclosure).

income.cgNote: S.C. Code § 12-6-1150 allows individuals a deduction equal to 44% of net capital gain (as defined in IRC § 1222, i.e. long-term). For 2026 (Act 110 of 2026, SC Information Letter #26-20): 1.99% on taxable income up to $29,999 and 5.21% of taxable income minus $966 from $30,000 (same brackets for all filing statuses); SC taxable income now starts from federal AGI and the federal standard/itemized deductions are replaced by the SC Income Adjusted Deduction. SC conforms to the IRC (as of 31 Dec 2024), so the federal § 121 home-sale exclusion carries through via federal AGI. Top rate was 6% for 2025.
income.cgShort: 44% of a long-term gain deducted

The $30,000 bracket threshold is the 2026 figure from IL #26-20; it is indexed yearly.

transfer.name: Real Estate Transfer Fee
transfer.rateText: Fifty cents for each five hundred dollars of value or fraction thereof upon the privilege of transferring title to real property (SDCL 43-4-21)
transfer.local: No local add-on is set by the statute; the fee is statewide.
transfer.payerNote: SDCL 43-4-21: the fee shall be paid by the grantor.

mortgageTax.note: Transfers solely to provide or release security for a debt are exempt from the transfer fee (SDCL 43-4-22(3)); no state mortgage recording tax found.

transfer.notes: SDCL 43-4-22 exempts, among others, gifts without consideration, transfers between spouses or parent and child for nominal consideration, divorce decrees, foreclosure deeds and corrective deeds.

income.cgNote: South Dakota does not impose a state income tax (SD Department of Revenue), so a gain on a home sale is not taxed by the state.
income.cgShort: no personal income tax

transfer.rateText: Property Transfer Tax: .37 per $100 (Knox County Register of Deeds fee schedule, collected by county registers for the state)
transfer.local: Collected by the county register of deeds at recording; no separate county transfer tax appears on the register fee schedules read (Knox, Shelby), only per-page recording fees.

mortgageTax.name: Mortgage (indebtedness) tax
mortgageTax.note: .115 per $100 of the indebtedness; the first $2,000 is exempt (Knox and Shelby County Register of Deeds fee schedules).

income.cgNote: Tennessee taxes neither wages nor capital gains: the Hall income tax (on interest and dividends only) was repealed for tax periods beginning on or after January 1, 2021 (TN Department of Revenue).
income.cgShort: no tax on wages or capital gains

transfer.local: The constitutional prohibition applies to any law, so counties and cities levy no transfer tax; only the county clerk's per-document recording fees apply.

mortgageTax.note: No mortgage recording tax found; only per-document recording fees.

transfer.notes: Art. VIII Sec. 29(b) still allows a tax on the issuance of title insurance and general business taxes.

income.cgNote: Flat 4.45% on state taxable income for taxable years beginning on or after January 1, 2026 (S.B. 60, 2026 General Session, retrospective operation; down from 4.5% in 2025). transfer.name: Property Transfer Tax (plus Clean Water Surcharge)
transfer.rateText: Principal residence of the buyer: 0.5% on the first $200,000 of value (no Clean Water Surcharge on that slice), then the general rate of 1.25% plus the 0.22% Clean Water Surcharge (total 1.47%) on value above $200,000. Other property: 1.25% + 0.22% = 1.47% of the whole value. Non-principal residence fit for year-round habitation that is not a long-term rental: 3.4% (3.62% with the surcharge). (32 V.S.A. §§ 9602, 9602a; Vermont Department of Taxes)
transfer.local: No local transfer tax; the tax and surcharge are state levies.

mortgageTax.note: No mortgage recording tax found.

transfer.notes: Brackets model a sale to a buyer who will use the home as principal residence. If the buyer gets a purchase money mortgage with a VHCB homeland grant or a VHFA/USDA Rural Development loan, the first $250,000 is exempt from both tax and surcharge. Second homes (year-round, not long-term rental) pay 3.4% + 0.22%. The tax also applies to transfers of a controlling interest in an entity owning Vermont property.

income.cgNote: 32 V.S.A. § 5811(21)(B)(ii): taxpayers may exclude either the first $5,000 of adjusted net capital gain or 40% of adjusted net capital gain from assets held more than three years, capped at 40% of federal taxable income or $350,000; but the 40% exclusion does not cover gains from the sale of real estate used as a primary or nonprimary residence (nor publicly traded stocks/bonds), so a home-sale gain can only use the flat $5,000 exclusion. Vermont starts from federal taxable income, so the federal § 121 exclusion carries through. A separate Vermont land gains tax (32 V.S.A. ch. 236) can apply to land held under six years.
income.cgShort: only the $5,000 exclusion applies to a home

transfer.name: State Recordation Tax on deeds + Grantor Tax
transfer.rateText: State recordation tax: 25 cents on every $100 or fraction thereof of the consideration or the assessed value, whichever is greater (Va. Code § 58.1-801) = 0.25%; plus grantor tax: 50 cents for each $500 or fraction thereof of the consideration or value, exclusive of liens remaining on the property (§ 58.1-802) = 0.10%. Combined state level 0.35%.
transfer.local: Cities and counties may add a local recordation tax equal to one-third of the state recordation tax (§ 58.1-814), i.e. about 0.0833% when levied. Half of the grantor tax goes to the locality. In member localities of the Northern Virginia Transportation Authority a regional WMATA capital fee of $0.10 per $100 (0.10%) is added, paid by the grantor (§ 58.1-802.3).
transfer.payerNote: Grantor tax (and the NoVA WMATA fee) shall be paid by the grantor (seller), though grantor and grantee may arrange for the grantee to pay (§ 58.1-802, § 58.1-802.3). § 58.1-801 does not name a payer for the state recordation tax on the deed.

mortgageTax.name: Recordation tax on deeds of trust or mortgages
mortgageTax.note: 25 cents per $100 of the obligation secured (§ 58.1-803), declining on tranches above $10 million; refinancing of debt already taxed pays 18 cents per $100 on the first $10 million. Localities may add one-third of the state tax (§ 58.1-814).

transfer.notes: Recordation tax applies to the greater of price or the most recent assessment. Grantor tax excludes the value of liens that remain on the property.

income.cgNote: Graduated 2% / 3% / 5% / 5.75%; 5.75% on Virginia taxable income over $17,000 for taxable years beginning on and after January 1, 1990 (Va. Code § 58.1-320), the same brackets for every filing status. No special capital gains rate: gains are taxed as ordinary income. Virginia starts from federal AGI, so the federal § 121 home-sale exclusion carries through.
income.cgShort: graduated rates, gain taxed as income

transfer.name: Real Estate Excise Tax (REET)
transfer.rateText: Graduated state REET on the selling price (RCW 82.45.060), current thresholds: $525,000 or less 1.10%; $525,000.01-$1,525,000 1.28%; $1,525,000.01-$3,025,000 2.75%; $3,025,000.01 or more 3%. For sales from January 1, 2027 the thresholds become $551,000 / $1,551,000 / $3,051,000 with the same rates.
transfer.local: Local REET must be added to the state rate; it varies by city/county location code and is published by DOR in periodic rate tables (e.g. 'Rates May 1, 2026 and after'). A $5 state technology fee applies to every transfer.
transfer.payerNote: Washington DOR: 'Usually, the seller pays this tax, but if they don't, the buyer is responsible'; unpaid tax can become a lien on the property.

mortgageTax.note: No mortgage recording tax found; the loan amount is not separately taxed (REET is on the full price).

transfer.notes: Thresholds are adjusted every four years (next change January 1, 2027). Agricultural and timberland pay a flat 1.28% state rate. Transfers of a controlling interest (50% or more within 36 months) in an entity owning Washington real property are subject to REET.

income.cgNote: Washington does not currently have an individual income tax (DOR). Its capital gains excise tax (RCW 82.87: 7% on Washington capital gains above a standard deduction of $278,000 for 2025, plus 2.9% on gains above $1,000,000 from 2025) exempts real estate, so a home-sale gain is not taxed. DOR announces a new 9.9% income tax on adjusted gross income above $1 million from January 1, 2028, which does not apply to 2026.
income.cgShort: capital gains excise tax exempts real estate

transfer.name: Excise Tax on the Privilege of Transferring Real Estate
transfer.rateText: State excise tax of $1.10 for each $500 value or fraction thereof (0.22%) plus the additional county excise tax of 55 cents for each $500 (0.11%), W. Va. Code § 11-22-2(a)-(b); total 0.33% at the base county rate.
transfer.local: The county tax is 55 cents per $500 (0.11%), but a county may raise it, up to $1.65 per $500 (0.33%) under § 11-22-2(b); with the state $1.10 the total can reach $2.75 per $500 (0.55%). 20% of the state tax collected is retained by the county.
transfer.payerNote: W. Va. Code § 11-22-2(b): the tax shall be paid by the grantor unless the grantee accepts the document without the tax having been paid, in which event it is paid by the grantee.

mortgageTax.note: No mortgage recording tax found in article 22.

transfer.notes: Only one state tax and one county tax are paid on any document, in the county where it is first recorded.

income.cgNote: For taxable years beginning on and after January 1, 2026 (W. Va. Code § 11-21-4j): 2.11% up to $10,000, 2.81%, 3.16%, 4.22%, and 4.58% over $60,000 (same table for single, joint and head of household; married filing separately 4.58% over $30,000). No special capital gains rate or exclusion found; WV taxable income starts from federal AGI, so the federal § 121 home-sale exclusion carries through.

estate.name: Connecticut
estate.notes: No tax up to the federal basic exclusion amount, then 12% of the excess; total tax capped at $15,000,000.

estate.name: District of Columbia
estate.notes: Graduated rates on the part above the exclusion, prorated when part of the estate lies outside DC.

estate.name: Hawaii
estate.notes: Exclusion subtracted first, then 10% to 20% on the rest; the exclusion is fixed at $5,490,000 and portable between spouses.

estate.name: Illinois
estate.notes: Interrelated calculation of the Attorney General: steep phase-in just above the threshold ($285,714 on a $5,000,000 estate), no portability.

estate.name: Maine
estate.notes: 8% on the next $3,000,000 above the exclusion, 10% on the following $3,000,000, 12% beyond.

estate.name: Maryland
estate.notes: 16% of the excess for most estates (the tax cannot exceed the old federal state death tax credit); Maryland portability allowed; inheritance tax paid is credited.

estate.name: Massachusetts
estate.notes: Old federal state death tax credit table on the estate less $60,000, minus a $99,600 credit: nothing up to $2,000,000, then 7.2% and up, no cliff.

estate.name: Minnesota
estate.notes: Exclusion subtracted first, then 13% to 16% on the rest; extra deduction for qualified small business and farm property.

estate.name: New York
estate.notes: Table on the whole estate; the credit shrinks between 100% and 105% of the exclusion and disappears above it (the cliff).

estate.name: Oregon
estate.notes: 10% from $1,000,000 rising to 16% above $9,500,000; the $1,000,000 threshold is not indexed and not portable.

estate.name: Rhode Island
estate.notes: Old federal state death tax credit table minus an $87,940 credit for 2026, which exempts the first $1,838,056; indexed each year.

estate.name: Vermont
estate.notes: 16% of the excess over $5,000,000, prorated to the Vermont share; taxable gifts within 2 years of death are added back.

estate.name: Washington
estate.notes: Deaths from July 1, 2026: $3,000,000 exclusion, 10% to 20%. Deaths January 1 to June 30, 2026: $3,076,000 and 10% to 35%.

inheritance.name: Kentucky

classes.who: Class A: spouse, parent, child, grandchild, brother, sister
Class B: niece, nephew, son- or daughter-in-law, aunt, uncle, great-grandchild
Class C: everyone else, such as cousins and friends

inheritance.notes: Kentucky sorts heirs into three classes. Class A, which covers the spouse, parents, children, grandchildren and siblings, pays nothing. Class B pays 4% to 16% after a $1,000 exemption, and Class C 6% to 16% after $500. A 5% discount applies if the tax is paid within nine months of the death, and Kentucky has no estate tax of its own.

inheritance.name: Maryland

classes.who: Spouse, parents, children and descendants, siblings, stepchildren, in-laws through a child
Everyone else: nieces, nephews, aunts, uncles, cousins, friends

inheritance.notes: Maryland is the only state with both an inheritance tax and an estate tax. The inheritance tax is a flat 10% of the clear value received by anyone outside the exempt circle of close family, and nothing is due when one person receives $1,000 or less. Life insurance paid to a named beneficiary is exempt. The tax is collected by the Register of Wills of the county and credited against the Maryland estate tax.

inheritance.name: Nebraska

classes.who: Parents, grandparents, siblings, children and other descendants
Uncles, aunts, nieces, nephews and their descendants

inheritance.notes: Nebraska cut its rates for deaths from 2023: close relatives pay 1% above $100,000, uncles, aunts, nieces and nephews 11% above $40,000, and everyone else 15% above $25,000. Any heir under 22 is exempt. The tax is a county tax, filed and paid in the county court where the estate is probated.

inheritance.name: New Jersey

classes.who: Class A: spouse or partner, parents, grandparents, children, stepchildren, grandchildren
Class C: brother or sister, son- or daughter-in-law
Class D: everyone else, such as nieces, nephews and friends
Class E: charities and public bodies

inheritance.notes: New Jersey repealed its estate tax for deaths from 2018 but kept the transfer inheritance tax. Class C heirs pay nothing on the first $25,000, then 11% to 16%; Class D heirs pay 15% on the first $700,000 and 16% above. Children and grandchildren are in Class A and pay nothing.

inheritance.name: Pennsylvania

classes.who: Surviving spouse, or parent inheriting from a child 21 or younger
Children, grandchildren, parents and other lineal heirs
Other heirs, such as nieces, nephews and friends

inheritance.notes: Pennsylvania taxes almost every inheritance outside the spouse: 4.5% for children and other lineal heirs, 12% for siblings and 15% for others, with no exemption amount. Property owned jointly by spouses is exempt, as is some farmland passed to family. The tax is due at death and a 5% discount applies when it is paid within three months.
